title: Four vendor answers, one that answers the question
intro:
*Five minutes. Commit before you look.*

You asked four vendors the same question: **"What evidence do you have that this tool does not produce disparate outcomes for a population like ours?"**

All four responded promptly and in good faith. All four sent something real.

**One of them answered the question you asked.** Find it.

Ask what each document is actually about, and what it would look like if the tool were unfair.

artifacts.label: Vendor A
artifacts.body: "We take fairness extremely seriously. Our platform is **ISO/IEC 42001 certified**, we maintain a documented AI governance framework covering the full model lifecycle, and our responsible AI committee reviews all model changes before release. I've attached our certification and our Responsible AI Principles. We're also SOC 2 Type II if that's helpful."

artifacts.label: Vendor B
artifacts.body: "Attached is our independent bias audit, completed February 2026 by a third-party firm. It covers selection rates by race and sex across our aggregate customer base, approximately 2.1 million applications, and reports four-fifths ratios above 0.8 for all groups measured. Our model has been updated twice since the audit; those releases were minor and we didn't consider re-audit necessary."

artifacts.label: Vendor C
artifacts.body: "Honestly. We don't have an audit on a population like yours, and I don't want to pretend otherwise. What we do have: our model card documents that we optimize for **structured interview performance ratings rather than similarity to current employees**; we publish our input features and we don't use zip code, school, or graduation year. We'll run a validation study on your applicant data during a paid pilot at our cost, on your definitions, and you own the output. And our standard contract commits us to producing the model version and configuration in effect on any date you specify, for seven years."

artifacts.label: Vendor D
artifacts.body: "Our model has been validated against job performance outcomes across 340 client deployments with a correlation of 0.34, significantly outperforming unstructured interviews. We've processed over 40 million candidate assessments. Our algorithm doesn't use protected characteristics as inputs, and we conduct ongoing internal monitoring for disparate impact."

options.label: C — no audit, but a pilot offer

reasoning:
**C answered the question, and it is the only one that did, while being the only one that admitted it had no audit.**

Work through what C actually supplied. **What it optimizes**, which is the highest-value answer in the module and the one nobody asks for: structured interview performance ratings rather than similarity to current employees. That is a design decision you can defend, disclosed without being pushed. **Its inputs**, published, and the explicit absence of zip code, school and graduation year, which are three of the most common proxies. **Evidence on a population like yours**, offered as a validation study on your applicant data, on your definitions, with you owning the output. And **the litigation question answered in the contract**: model version and configuration reproducible on any specified date, for seven years.

That last item is the tell of a vendor that has thought about being subpoenaed alongside you. It costs them real engineering to promise and it is worth more than any audit in the set.

The honesty isn't a soft factor either. **"We do not have that, and I do not want to pretend otherwise"** is a vendor whose other claims you can weigh, which is a different commercial relationship from one where every answer is yes.

**A changed the subject.** ISO/IEC 42001 certifies an AI management system (governance, roles, controls, review) not the fairness of a model. SOC 2 is about security and availability controls and is even further from the question. All of it is genuine evidence of something else, and the substitution is almost certainly unintentional: asked "is it fair?", a salesperson reached for the most rigorous document available.

**B is the closest miss and the most instructive.** A real independent audit is more than most vendors have. But it reports four-fifths ratios **with no significance test**, on the vendor's **aggregate customer base** rather than a population like yours — 2.1 million applications tells you about their book, not your applicant pool for your role in your region — and the model has been **updated twice since**, which fails Module 3's recency criterion. "We didn't consider re-audit necessary" is the vendor grading its own changes.

**D is a validity claim wearing a fairness claim's clothes, and it is the most sophisticated failure.** A 0.34 correlation with performance is a respectable *validity* figure and says nothing about disparate impact, a tool can predict performance well and still select groups at very different rates. "Outperforming unstructured interviews" is a comparison against nearly the weakest method available. Forty million assessments is a volume figure, not a sample. And **"does not use protected characteristics as inputs"** is the proxy misunderstanding stated as a reassurance: no competent tool uses them directly, and Module 3 exists because the disparity travels through zip code, graduation year and commute distance instead.
